alerts.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 28 at 3:48AM HST until September 28 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR SOUTH FACING SHORES OF ALL
HAWAIIAN ISLANDS...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR WEST FACING SHORES OF THE BIG
ISLAND...

.Rough short to medium period south-southwest swell from
Hurricane Nolo is expected to generate a quick pulse of advisory
level surf for south facing shores of all islands and west facing
shores of the Big Island today. While this is currently forecast
to gradually fade below advisory thresholds tonight, there is some
uncertainty in how quickly this will occur and it is possible
that advisory level surf may persist through Tuesday even as the
swell becomes southwesterly.

* WHAT...For south facing shores, large surf becoming 7 to 10 ft
today. For west facing shores of the Big Island, large surf
becoming 6 to 8 ft today.

* WHERE...West facing shores of the Big Island and south facing
shores of all Hawaiian Islands (excluding Southeast Big Island).

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
alerts.instruction:
Heed all advice from ocean safety officials. When in doubt, don't
go out.

alerts.description:
* WHAT...East winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of Maui, Molokai, Oahu, and the Big Island.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Winds this strong can tear off shingles, knock down tree
branches, blow away tents and awnings and make it difficult to
steer, especially for drivers of high profile vehicles.

sure tents and awnings are secure or take them down. Be prepared for
power outages.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM HST Mon Sep 28 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located about 100 miles southwest of Cabo San Lazaro, Mexico,
on Hurricane Nolo, located a few hundred miles southwest of the main
Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical Storm Rachel, located a few
hundred miles south-southwest of Acapulco, Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (EP91):
A broad area of low pressure located well east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands continues to become better organized. Environmental
conditions are conducive for further development, and a tropical
depression is expected to form later today or tomorrow. The system
should move generally northeastward and remain well east of the
Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

aiBriefing: Obecnie na Hawajach obowiązują ostrzeżenia o silnym przyboju i wietrze, ale wygasają one już dziś wieczorem (28 września), czyli 3 dni przed Waszym wylotem 2 października — nie powinny dotyczyć Waszej podróży. Ważniejszy jest huragan Nolo, kategoria 4, znajdujący się obecnie zaledwie ok. 656 km od trasy — to on odpowiada za dzisiejsze ostrzeżenia o falach. Do czasu Waszego przylotu sytuacja może się zmienić, więc warto śledzić jego rozwój w najbliższych dniach. Dodatkowo CPHC wskazuje na 90% szans powstania nowego systemu w ciągu 7 dni daleko na wschód-południowy wschód od wysp, ale trasa tego systemu ma prowadzić z dala od Hawajów. Poziom zagrożenia 'Podwyższony' odzwierciedla bliskość aktywnego huraganu, nie bezpośrednie zagrożenie dla Waszych dat — warto sprawdzić prognozę ponownie bliżej wylotu.
